findings_and_questions.classification: conditional current source-backed geometry/identity contract question; central adjudicates any new repair unit
findings_and_questions.first_contract: InteriorField::from_plan computes a room opening contribution and opening_light searches all retained opening assemblies for the first TimberShutter whose frame origin lies within 0.01 m of the unprojected source WallSegment centre and whose sill matches. If the corresponding retained shutter frame lies beyond that tolerance and no other shutter at that centre/sill matches, the function returns no opaque ID: the contribution uses the transmitting-window baseline and no ShutterLight entry is created to follow that shutter.
findings_and_questions.evidence_and_condition: The storey wall producer retains span.centre plus a tangent opening offset as its assembly origin; the span computes endpoints with exterior upper-storey projection and may shift its centre along the wall at returns. These terms can move the assembly origin away from the original WallSegment centre. The observed generator closure policy selects a TimberShutter for qualifying FachwerkCottage opening IDs, but the ordinary inspected Cottage program is one storey with zero projection; other inspected projected default archetypes do not establish shutter selection. No supported generated plan combining a sufficient shift with an eligible shutter has been proved, and another matching candidate could change the outcome. No product, fixture or visual behavior was executed.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Trace actual admitted program variants and generated identity correspondence, including corner-bond shifts and exterior projection, then use an explicit authoritative opening-to-assembly association or a geometry-aware policy that retains legitimate shifted apertures and rejects ambiguous/missing mappings. Preserve separate baseline glass transmission and opaque shutter semantics.
relationships: The prior ASSESSMENT-INTERIOR-LIGHTING-95E and 059 L12-CLOSURE-SCENE-WINDOW-NATIVE-PROJECTION-LIGHTING retain broader projection/lighting obligations; this bounded field matching mechanism is related, not an automatic duplicate or historic finding.
Related to P16-WINDOW-OPENING-FRAME-AGGREGATE and closure reference source ownership; this issue is the field producer match, not necessarily the same first failed contract.

Exact pinned normalize_or_zero implementation, transform mutation/replication/parenting, and what a degenerate pose should mean are not independently proven. No runtime inference.

lenses.bounded_assessment: Shutter source contains no raw domain-string API. recipe_mesh native attribute constants and expect messages are native format/diagnostic material, not evidence of status classification by prose.

Aperture tolerance, closure angle and projection matching encode independent policies. The 0.01 m source-origin tolerance is not an identity; native vertex indices and cache float-bit keys have different roles.

OpeningAssemblyId and SceneBuildingId are retained for shutters; the untyped openness float and `(usize, LightSample)` contribution pairs are retained between producer and consumer. Decide local owner from actual bounds and tolerances, not by blanket wrapping.

SceneWindow keeps checked SpatialDirection and LeafDimensions into native transform and rendering boundary. Retain their checked values and frames while recognizing a newly computed openness ratio and native position/normal/UV arrays.

Aperture opening identity, room-cell contribution index, positive/negative light lobes, and scene building identity are distinct concepts. A single opening ID does not automatically prove global identity across scenes.

Each updated sample begins from base and accumulates each stored contribution once, then caps RGB; inputs and indices depend on the producer. Origin geometry comparison, transform normalization, bounded ratio, and tangent generation require separate numeric policies.

LodMesh indices reference a separately stored vertex list. A ShutterLight contribution index must remain in bounds of samples/base_samples; this construction copies samples as base and derives indices in the same loop, while later mutation and accepted plan bounds remain unproved.

Public LodMesh serde does not encode index-to-vertex coherence. SceneWindow leaf serde admits finite/normalized leaves individually, but independent GlobalTransform and multi-entity ID relationships remain external contracts.

WindowLeafKind, WindowBarPresence, material role and missing-closure errors retain distinct modes. No assertion that shutters and glass share identical transmission or that missing window must be open.

Opening source wall, retained assembly frame, shutter contribution ID and replicated entity independently represent related geometry; matching by approximate origin and sill requires an explicit authority/relationship. Base and current sample arrays serve different update roles.

Individual P16 source objects equal pinned 95e bytes, not entire dirty snapshot state. Preserve glass transmission, opaque baseline policy, thresholded change flag, room ID in positive.w, native attribute order and material-specific tangent generation.

Scene window IDs and checked directions survive to native transform openness; computed ratio is new numerical state. 774 TRACE-004 treats actual mesh packing and dot/normalization as native boundaries while historical F009 separately concerns unchanged checked glazing dimensions through Builder.

LodMesh and LodVertex derive serde; SceneWindow uses custom admission to retain contextual geometry errors. Nothing inspected justifies replacing custom admission or asserting independent raw containers prove coherent aggregate validity.
